messages: The upper ice waterline displacement shall equal the greatest linked waterline case displacement, within a relative tolerance of 1e-6 and an absolute fallback of 1e-9 kt.
intended.query:
PREFIX nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#>
            PREFIX qudt: <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/>
            PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>

            SELECT $this ?duiValue ?caseValue
            WHERE {
                $this nltl:upperIceWaterlineDisplacement ?duiNode ;
                       nltl:hasUpperIceWaterlineCase ?caseNode .
                ?duiNode qudt:numericValue ?duiValue .
                ?caseNode nltl:waterlineCaseDisplacement ?caseDisplacementNode .
                ?caseDisplacementNode qudt:numericValue ?caseValue .

                FILTER NOT EXISTS {
                    $this nltl:hasUpperIceWaterlineCase ?greaterCaseNode .
                    ?greaterCaseNode nltl:waterlineCaseDisplacement ?greaterDisplacementNode .
                    ?greaterDisplacementNode qudt:numericValue ?greaterValue .
                    FILTER (?greaterValue > ?caseValue)
                }

                FILTER (
                    ABS(?duiValue - ?caseValue) >
                    (0.000001 * ABS(?caseValue) + 0.000000001)
                )
            }

evidence.excerpt:
In the case of longitudinally-framed plating (  20 deg), when b < s, the net thickness is
         given by:

             tnet = 500 ꞏ s ꞏ ((AF ꞏ PPFp ꞏ Pavg) / y)0.5 ꞏ (2 ꞏ b / s – (b / s)2)0.5 / (1 + s / (2 ꞏ l)) [mm]


         In the case of obliquely-framed plating (70 deg >  > 20 deg), linear interpolation is to be
         used.

             where  = smallest angle between the chord of the waterline and the line of the first
                   level framing as illustrated in Figure 3 [deg].
                   s = transverse frame spacing in transversely-framed ships or longitudinal frame
                   spacing in longitudinally-framed ships [m]
evidence.review_note: Longitudinal <=20 degrees, b>=s and b<s branches and square-root term match; declared complex-readiness scope.

intended.query:
PREFIX nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#>
            PREFIX qudt: <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/>
            PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>

            SELECT $this
            WHERE {
                ?ship a nltl:ship ;
                      nltl:polarClass ?pc ;
                      nltl:hasSteelGradeRequirementCase $this .
                $this nltl:asBuiltPlateThickness ?thicknessNode ;
                      nltl:steelMaterialClass ?material ;
                      nltl:steelStrengthCategory ?strength ;
                      nltl:actualHullStructuralSteelGrade ?actual .
                ?thicknessNode qudt:numericValue ?thickness .
                BIND(
                    IF(?thickness <= 10, 1,
                    IF(?thickness <= 15, 2,
                    IF(?thickness <= 20, 3,
                    IF(?thickness <= 25, 4,
                    IF(?thickness <= 30, 5,
                    IF(?thickness <= 35, 6,
                    IF(?thickness <= 40, 7,
                    IF(?thickness <= 45, 8,
                    IF(?thickness <= 50, 9, 0)))))))))
                    AS ?band
                )
                BIND((?pc IN (nltl:polarClassPc1, nltl:polarClassPc2, nltl:polarClassPc3)) AS ?pc13)
                BIND((?pc IN (nltl:polarClassPc1, nltl:polarClassPc2, nltl:polarClassPc3, nltl:polarClassPc4, nltl:polarClassPc5)) AS ?pc15)
                BIND((?pc IN (nltl:polarClassPc4, nltl:polarClassPc5)) AS ?pc45)
                BIND((?pc IN (nltl:polarClassPc6, nltl:polarClassPc7)) AS ?pc67)

                BIND(
                    IF(
                        (
                            ?strength = nltl:normalStrengthSteelCategory &&
                            (
                                (?band = 1 && ?material IN (nltl:steelMaterialClassOne, nltl:steelMaterialClassTwo)) ||
                                (?band >= 2 && ?band <= 4 && ?pc67 && ?material IN (nltl:steelMaterialClassOne, nltl:steelMaterialClassTwo)) ||
                                (?band >= 5 && ?band <= 6 && ?pc67 && ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassOne)
                            )
                        ),
                        nltl:steelGradeB,
                        IF(
                            (
                                ?strength = nltl:normalStrengthSteelCategory &&
                                (
                                    (?band >= 2 && ?band <= 4 && ?pc15 && ?material IN (nltl:steelMaterialClassOne, nltl:steelMaterialClassTwo)) ||
                                    (?band >= 5 && ?band <= 8 && ?pc15 && ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassTwo) ||
                                    (?band >= 5 && ?band <= 8 && ?pc67 && ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassTwo) ||
                                    (?band = 9 && ?pc67 && ?material IN (nltl:steelMaterialClassOne, nltl:steelMaterialClassTwo))
                                )
                            ),
                            nltl:steelGradeD,
                            IF(
                                (
                                    ?strength = nltl:normalStrengthSteelCategory &&
                                    (
                                        (?band = 1 && ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassThree && ?pc15) ||
                                        (?band >= 2 && ?band <= 4 && ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassThree && ?pc15) ||
                                        (?band >= 5 && ?band <= 8 && ?material IN (nltl:steelMaterialClassTwo, nltl:steelMaterialClassThree) && ?pc15) ||
                                        (?band >= 5 && ?band <= 8 && ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassThree && ?pc67) ||
                                        (?band = 9 && ?material IN (nltl:steelMaterialClassOne, nltl:steelMaterialClassTwo) && ?pc15) ||
                                        (?band = 9 && ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassThree && ?pc67)
                                    )
                                ),
                                nltl:steelGradeE,
                                IF(
                                    (
                                        ?strength = nltl:highTensileSteelCategory &&
                                        (
                                            (?band >= 1 && ?band <= 4 && ?material IN (nltl:steelMaterialClassOne, nltl:steelMaterialClassTwo)) ||
                                            (?band = 1 && ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassThree && ?pc67) ||
                                            (?band >= 5 && ?band <= 9 && ?material IN (nltl:steelMaterialClassOne, nltl:steelMaterialClassTwo) && ?pc67)
                                        )
                                    ),
                                    nltl:steelGradeAh,
                                    IF(
                                        (
                                            ?strength = nltl:highTensileSteelCategory &&
                                            (
                                                (?band >= 2 && ?band <= 4 && ?pc15 && ?material IN (nltl:steelMaterialClassOne, nltl:steelMaterialClassTwo)) ||
                                                (?band >= 2 && ?band <= 4 && ?pc67 && ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassThree) ||
                                                (?band >= 5 && ?band <= 8 && ?pc15 && ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassOne) ||
                                                (?band >= 5 && ?band <= 8 && ?pc15 && ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassTwo) ||
                                                (?band = 9 && ?pc15 && ?material IN (nltl:steelMaterialClassOne, nltl:steelMaterialClassTwo))
                                            )
                                        ),
                                        nltl:steelGradeDh,
                                        IF(
                                            (
                                                ?strength = nltl:highTensileSteelCategory &&
                                                (
                                                    (?band >= 1 && ?band <= 4 && ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassThree && ?pc15) ||
                                                    (?band >= 5 && ?band <= 8 && ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassTwo && ?pc15) ||
                                                    (?band >= 5 && ?band <= 8 && ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassThree) ||
                                                    (?band = 9 && ?pc15 && ?material IN (nltl:steelMaterialClassOne, nltl:steelMaterialClassTwo)) ||
                                                    (?band = 9 && ?pc67 && ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassThree)
                                                )
                                            ),
                                            nltl:steelGradeEh,
                                            IF(
                                                (
                                                    ?strength = nltl:highTensileSteelCategory &&
                                                    ?material = nltl:steelMaterialClassThree &&
                                                    (
                                                        (?band >= 7 && ?band <= 8 && ?pc13) ||
                                                        (?band = 9 && (?pc13 || ?pc45))
                                                    )
                                                ),
                                                nltl:steelGradeFh,
                                                nltl:benchmarkEntity
                                            )
                                        )
                                    )
                                )
                            )
                        )
                    )
                    AS ?expected
                )

                OPTIONAL {
                    $this nltl:requiredHullStructuralSteelGrade ?required .
                }

                OPTIONAL {
                    ?actual nltl:steelGradeOrderRank ?actualRank .
                }

                FILTER(
                    ?expected = nltl:benchmarkEntity ||
                    !BOUND(?required) ||
                    ?required != ?expected ||
                    !BOUND(?actualRank) ||
                    EXISTS {
                        ?required nltl:steelGradeOrderRank ?requiredRank .
                        FILTER(?actualRank < ?requiredRank)
                    } ||
                    (
                        ?strength = nltl:normalStrengthSteelCategory &&
                        ?actual NOT IN (
                            nltl:steelGradeB,
                            nltl:steelGradeD,
                            nltl:steelGradeE
                        )
                    ) ||
                    (
                        ?strength = nltl:highTensileSteelCategory &&
                        ?actual NOT IN (
                            nltl:steelGradeAh,
                            nltl:steelGradeDh,
                            nltl:steelGradeEh,
                            nltl:steelGradeFh
                        )
                    )
                )
            }

evidence.excerpt:
3.3.2    In order to comply with the functional requirements of paragraph 3.2.2 above, the
following applies:

        .1       scantlings of category A ships shall be approved by the Administration, or a
                 recognized organization accepted by it, taking into account standards
                 acceptable to the Organization or other standards offering an equivalent
                 level of safety;

        .2       scantlings of category B ships shall be approved by the Administration, or a
                 recognized organization accepted by it, taking into account standards
                 acceptable to the Organization or other standards offering an equivalent
                 level of safety;

        .3       scantlings of ice strengthened category C ships shall be approved by the
                 Administration, or a recognized organization accepted by it, taking into
                 account acceptable standards adequate for the ice types and
                 concentrations encountered in the area of operation; and

        .4       a category C ship need not be ice strengthened if, in the opinion of the
                 Administration, the ship's structure is adequate for its intended operation.
                         RESOLUTION MSC.385(94) (adopted on 21 November 2014)
                    INTERNATIONAL CODE FOR SHIPS OPERATING IN POLAR WATERS
                                         (POLAR CODE)

                                             - 17 -

4.3.1.1 In order to comply with the functional requirement of paragraph 4.2.1, for ships

                  water plane; and

         .3       the projected lateral area of discontinuous surfaces of rail, sundry booms,
                  spars (except masts) and rigging of ships having no sails and the projected
                  lateral area of other small objects shall be computed by increasing the total
                  projected area of continuous surfaces by 5% and the static moments of this
                  area by 10%.

shall be:

         .1       designed to minimize the accretion of ice; and

         .2      equipped with such means for removing ice as the Administration may
                 require; for example, electrical and pneumatic devices, and/or special tools
                 such as axes or wooden clubs for removing ice from bulwarks, rails and
                 erections.

source_evidence.frozen_requirement_text: For ships operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur, the following icing allowance shall be made in the stability calculations: 30 kg/m^2 on exposed weather decks and gangways; 7.5 kg/m^2 for the projected lateral area of each side of the ship above the water plane; and the projected lateral area of discontinuous surfaces of rail, sundry booms, spars (except masts) and rigging of ships having no sails and the projected lateral area of other small objects shall be computed by increasing the total projected area of continuous surfaces by 5% and the static moments of this area by 10%.

evidence.excerpt:
4.3.1.1 In order to comply with the functional requirement of paragraph 4.2.1, for ships
operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur, the following
icing allowance shall be made in the stability calculations:

         .1       30 kg/m2 on exposed weather decks and gangways;

         .2       7.5 kg/m2 for the projected lateral area of each side of the ship above the
                  water plane; and

         .3       the projected lateral area of discontinuous surfaces of rail, sundry booms,
                  spars (except masts) and rigging of ships having no sails and the projected
                  lateral area of other small objects shall be computed by increasing the total
                  projected area of continuous surfaces by 5% and the static moments of this
                  area by 10%.

4.3.1.2 Ships operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur
shall be:

         .1       designed to minimize the accretion of ice; and

         .2      equipped with such means for removing ice as the Administration may
                 require; for example, electrical and pneumatic devices, and/or special tools
                 such as axes or wooden clubs for removing ice from bulwarks, rails and
                 erections.
evidence.review_note: When accretion likely: 30kg/m2 decks, 7.5kg/m2 sides, small-object area +5% and moments +10%.

source_evidence.frozen_requirement_text: For ships operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur, the following icing allowance shall be made in the stability calculations: 30 kg/m^2 on exposed weather decks and gangways; 7.5 kg/m^2 for the projected lateral area of each side of the ship above the water plane; and the projected lateral area of discontinuous surfaces of rail, sundry booms, spars (except masts) and rigging of ships having no sails and the projected lateral area of other small objects shall be computed by increasing the total projected area of continuous surfaces by 5% and the static moments of this area by 10%.

contract.comparisonModel: IF ice_accretion_likely = true, THEN deck_icing_allowance_kg_m2 = 30, side_icing_allowance_kg_m2 = 7.5, discontinuous_surface_projected_area = continuous_surface_projected_area * 1.05, and discontinuous_surface_static_moment = continuous_surface_static_moment * 1.10.

evidence.excerpt:
4.3.1.1 In order to comply with the functional requirement of paragraph 4.2.1, for ships
operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur, the following
icing allowance shall be made in the stability calculations:

         .1       30 kg/m2 on exposed weather decks and gangways;

         .2       7.5 kg/m2 for the projected lateral area of each side of the ship above the
                  water plane; and

         .3       the projected lateral area of discontinuous surfaces of rail, sundry booms,
                  spars (except masts) and rigging of ships having no sails and the projected
                  lateral area of other small objects shall be computed by increasing the total
                  projected area of continuous surfaces by 5% and the static moments of this
                  area by 10%.

4.3.1.2 Ships operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur
shall be:

         .1       designed to minimize the accretion of ice; and

         .2      equipped with such means for removing ice as the Administration may
                 require; for example, electrical and pneumatic devices, and/or special tools
                 such as axes or wooden clubs for removing ice from bulwarks, rails and
                 erections.
evidence.review_note: When accretion likely: 30kg/m2 decks, 7.5kg/m2 sides, small-object area +5% and moments +10%.

source_evidence.frozen_requirement_text: For ships operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur, the following icing allowance shall be made in the stability calculations: 30 kg/m^2 on exposed weather decks and gangways; 7.5 kg/m^2 for the projected lateral area of each side of the ship above the water plane; and the projected lateral area of discontinuous surfaces of rail, sundry booms, spars (except masts) and rigging of ships having no sails and the projected lateral area of other small objects shall be computed by increasing the total projected area of continuous surfaces by 5% and the static moments of this area by 10%.

contract.comparisonModel: IF ice_accretion_likely = true, THEN deck_icing_allowance_kg_m2 = 30, side_icing_allowance_kg_m2 = 7.5, discontinuous_surface_projected_area = continuous_surface_projected_area * 1.05, and discontinuous_surface_static_moment = continuous_surface_static_moment * 1.10.

evidence.excerpt:
4.3.1.1 In order to comply with the functional requirement of paragraph 4.2.1, for ships
operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur, the following
icing allowance shall be made in the stability calculations:

         .1       30 kg/m2 on exposed weather decks and gangways;

         .2       7.5 kg/m2 for the projected lateral area of each side of the ship above the
                  water plane; and

         .3       the projected lateral area of discontinuous surfaces of rail, sundry booms,
                  spars (except masts) and rigging of ships having no sails and the projected
                  lateral area of other small objects shall be computed by increasing the total
                  projected area of continuous surfaces by 5% and the static moments of this
                  area by 10%.

4.3.1.2 Ships operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur
shall be:

         .1       designed to minimize the accretion of ice; and

         .2      equipped with such means for removing ice as the Administration may
                 require; for example, electrical and pneumatic devices, and/or special tools
                 such as axes or wooden clubs for removing ice from bulwarks, rails and
                 erections.
evidence.review_note: When accretion likely: 30kg/m2 decks, 7.5kg/m2 sides, small-object area +5% and moments +10%.

evidence.excerpt:
4.3.1.1 In order to comply with the functional requirement of paragraph 4.2.1, for ships
operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur, the following
icing allowance shall be made in the stability calculations:

         .1       30 kg/m2 on exposed weather decks and gangways;

         .2       7.5 kg/m2 for the projected lateral area of each side of the ship above the
                  water plane; and

         .3       the projected lateral area of discontinuous surfaces of rail, sundry booms,
                  spars (except masts) and rigging of ships having no sails and the projected
                  lateral area of other small objects shall be computed by increasing the total
                  projected area of continuous surfaces by 5% and the static moments of this
                  area by 10%.

4.3.1.2 Ships operating in areas and during periods where ice accretion is likely to occur
shall be:

         .1       designed to minimize the accretion of ice; and

         .2      equipped with such means for removing ice as the Administration may
                 require; for example, electrical and pneumatic devices, and/or special tools
                 such as axes or wooden clubs for removing ice from bulwarks, rails and
                 erections.

messages: Longitudinal and vertical damage extents must satisfy the specified piecewise formulas.
intended.query:
PREFIX nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#>
            PREFIX qudt: <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/>
            PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
            PREFIX sh: <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#>
            SELECT $this
            WHERE {
                $this nltl:damageCenterForwardOfMaxBreadth ?forward ;
                      nltl:upperIceWaterlineLength ?lengthNode ;
                      nltl:upperIceWaterlineDraught ?draughtNode ;
                      nltl:longitudinalDamageExtent ?longNode ;
                      nltl:verticalDamageExtent ?verticalNode .

                ?lengthNode qudt:numericValue ?length .
                ?draughtNode qudt:numericValue ?draught .
                ?longNode qudt:numericValue ?longitudinal .
                ?verticalNode qudt:numericValue ?vertical .

                BIND(IF(?forward = true,
                        "0.045"^^xsd:decimal * ?length,
                        "0.015"^^xsd:decimal * ?length) AS ?expectedLongitudinal)
                BIND(IF("0.20"^^xsd:decimal * ?draught < ?expectedLongitudinal,
                        "0.20"^^xsd:decimal * ?draught,
                        ?expectedLongitudinal) AS ?expectedVertical)

                FILTER (
                    ABS(?longitudinal - ?expectedLongitudinal) >
                    IF(
                        ABS(?expectedLongitudinal) * "0.000001"^^xsd:decimal >
                        "0.000000001"^^xsd:decimal,
                        ABS(?expectedLongitudinal) * "0.000001"^^xsd:decimal,
                        "0.000000001"^^xsd:decimal
                    )
                    ||
                    ABS(?vertical - ?expectedVertical) >
                    IF(
                        ABS(?expectedVertical) * "0.000001"^^xsd:decimal >
                        "0.000000001"^^xsd:decimal,
                        ABS(?expectedVertical) * "0.000001"^^xsd:decimal,
                        "0.000000001"^^xsd:decimal
                    )
                )
            }

intended.query:
PREFIX nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#>
            PREFIX qudt: <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/>
            PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>

            SELECT $this
            WHERE {
                $this nltl:damageCenterForwardOfMaxBreadth ?forward ;
                      nltl:upperIceWaterlineLength ?lengthNode ;
                      nltl:upperIceWaterlineDraught ?draughtNode ;
                      nltl:longitudinalDamageExtent ?longitudinalNode ;
                      nltl:verticalDamageExtent ?verticalNode ;
                      nltl:selectedVerticalDamagePosition ?positionNode .

                ?lengthNode qudt:numericValue ?length .
                ?draughtNode qudt:numericValue ?draught .
                ?longitudinalNode qudt:numericValue ?longitudinal .
                ?verticalNode qudt:numericValue ?vertical .
                ?positionNode qudt:numericValue ?position .

                BIND(IF(?forward = true,
                        ?length * 0.045,
                        ?length * 0.015) AS ?expectedLongitudinal)
                BIND(IF(?draught * 0.20 < ?expectedLongitudinal,
                        ?draught * 0.20,
                        ?expectedLongitudinal) AS ?expectedVertical)
                BIND((?expectedLongitudinal * 0.000001) + 0.000000001 AS ?longitudinalTolerance)
                BIND((?expectedVertical * 0.000001) + 0.000000001 AS ?verticalTolerance)

                FILTER (

                    ?longitudinal > (?expectedLongitudinal + ?longitudinalTolerance) ||
                    ?vertical < (?expectedVertical - ?verticalTolerance) ||
                    ?vertical > (?expectedVertical + ?verticalTolerance) ||
                    ?position < 0.0 ||
                    ?position > (?draught * 1.20)
                )
            }

PREFIX nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#>
            PREFIX qudt: <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/>
            PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
            PREFIX sh: <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#>
            SELECT $this
            WHERE {
                $this nltl:damageCenterForwardOfMaxBreadth ?forward ;
                      nltl:upperIceWaterlineLength ?lengthNode ;
                      nltl:upperIceWaterlineDraught ?draughtNode ;
                      nltl:longitudinalDamageExtent ?longNode ;
                      nltl:verticalDamageExtent ?verticalNode .

                ?lengthNode qudt:numericValue ?length .
                ?draughtNode qudt:numericValue ?draught .
                ?longNode qudt:numericValue ?longitudinal .
                ?verticalNode qudt:numericValue ?vertical .

                BIND(IF(?forward = true,
                        "0.045"^^xsd:decimal * ?length,
                        "0.015"^^xsd:decimal * ?length) AS ?expectedLongitudinal)
                BIND(IF("0.20"^^xsd:decimal * ?draught < ?expectedLongitudinal,
                        "0.20"^^xsd:decimal * ?draught,
                        ?expectedLongitudinal) AS ?expectedVertical)

                FILTER (
                    ABS(?longitudinal - ?expectedLongitudinal) >
                    IF(
                        ABS(?expectedLongitudinal) * "0.000001"^^xsd:decimal >
                        "0.000000001"^^xsd:decimal,
                        ABS(?expectedLongitudinal) * "0.000001"^^xsd:decimal,
                        "0.000000001"^^xsd:decimal
                    )
                    ||
                    ABS(?vertical - ?expectedVertical) >
                    IF(
                        ABS(?expectedVertical) * "0.000001"^^xsd:decimal >
                        "0.000000001"^^xsd:decimal,
                        ABS(?expectedVertical) * "0.000001"^^xsd:decimal,
                        "0.000000001"^^xsd:decimal
                    )
                )
            }

paragraph 4.3.2.1 shall be such that:

         .1      the longitudinal extent is 4.5% of the upper ice waterline length if centred
                 forward of the maximum breadth on the upper ice waterline, and 1.5% of
                 upper ice waterline length otherwise, and shall be assumed at any
                 longitudinal position along the ship's length;

         .2      the transverse penetration extent is 760 mm, measured normal to the shell
                 over the full extent of the damage; and

         .3      the vertical extent is the lesser of 20% of the upper ice waterline draught or
                 the longitudinal extent, and shall be assumed at any vertical position
                 between the keel and 120% of the upper ice waterline draught.


              CHAPTER 5 – WATERTIGHT AND WEATHERTIGHT INTEGRITY

5.1      Goal

The goal of this chapter is to provide measures to maintain watertight and weathertight
integrity.

5.2      Functional requirements

intended.query:
PREFIX nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#>
            PREFIX qudt: <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/>
            PREFIX unit: <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/>
            PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>

            SELECT $this
            WHERE {
                $this nltl:hasComponent ?pump .
                ?pump a ?pumpType .
                FILTER (
                    ?pumpType IN (
                        nltl:firePump,
                        nltl:emergencyFirePump,
                        nltl:waterMistPump,
                        nltl:waterSprayPump
                    )
                )
                FILTER NOT EXISTS {
                    ?pump nltl:hasContainingCompartment ?compartment .
                    ?compartment nltl:maintainedTemperature ?quantity .
                    ?quantity qudt:numericValue ?value ;
                              qudt:unit unit:DEG_C .
                    FILTER (
                        datatype(?value) = xsd:decimal &&
                        ?value > 0
                    )
                }
            }

IMO-123-N-F01.intended_rationale: Residue is recoverable by commonly available unloading methods.

source_evidence.frozen_requirement_text: Discharge of cargo residues that cannot be recovered using commonly available methods for unloading shall only be permitted while the ship is en route and where all of the following conditions are satisfied: cargo residues, cleaning agents or additives, contained in hold washing water do not include any substances classified as harmful to the marine environment; both the port of departure and the next port of destination are within Arctic waters and the ship will not transit outside Arctic waters between those ports; no adequate reception facilities are available at those ports; and discharge of cargo hold washing water containing residues shall be made as far as practicable from areas of ice concentration exceeding 1/10, but in any case not less than 12 nautical miles from the nearest land, nearest ice shelf, or nearest fast ice.

contract.comparisonModel: Cargo-residue discharge is permitted only if residue_not_recoverable_by_common_methods = true, ship_en_route = true, harmful_substance_present = false, departure_and_destination_within_Arctic = true, route_remains_within_Arctic = true, adequate_reception_facilities_available = false, and distance_to_nearest_land_ice_shelf_or_fast_ice_nm >= 12; record distance from ice concentration greater than 1/10. Both discharge distances are represented on each applicable dischargeDistanceRecords node; distanceToNearestLandIceShelfOrFastIce is at least 12 nautical miles and no numerical minimum is imposed for the ice-concentration-area distance.

evidence.excerpt:
.5       discharge of cargo residues that cannot be recovered using commonly
                 available methods for unloading shall only be permitted while the ship is
                 en route and where all of the following conditions are satisfied:
                 .1         cargo residues, cleaning agents or additives, contained in hold
                            washing water do not include any substances classified as harmful
                            to the marine environment, taking into account guidelines
                            developed by the Organization;
                           RESOLUTION MSC.385(94) (adopted on 21 November 2014)
                      INTERNATIONAL CODE FOR SHIPS OPERATING IN POLAR WATERS
                                           (POLAR CODE)

                                               - 43 -

                 .2         both the port of departure and the next port of destination are
                            within Arctic waters and the ship will not transit outside Arctic
                            waters between those ports;

                 .3         no adequate reception facilities are available at those ports, taking
                            into account guidelines developed by the Organization; and

                 .4         where the conditions of subparagraphs 5.2.1.5.1, 5.2.1.5.2
                            and 5.2.1.5.3 of this paragraph have been fulfilled, discharge of
                            cargo hold washing water containing residues shall be made as far
                            as practicable from areas of ice concentration exceeding 1/10, but
                            in any case not less than 12 nautical miles from the nearest land,
                            nearest ice shelf, or nearest fast ice.

5.2.2    In the Antarctic area, discharge of garbage into the sea permitted in accordance with
regulation 6 of MARPOL Annex V shall meet the following additional requirements:

        .1       discharges under regulation 6.1 of MARPOL Annex V shall be as far as
                 practicable from areas of ice concentration exceeding 1/10, but in any case
                 not less than 12 nautical miles from the nearest fast ice; and

        .2       food waste shall not be discharged onto ice.

5.2.3  Operation in polar waters shall be taken into account, as appropriate, in the
Garbage Record Book, Garbage Management Plan and the placards as required by
MARPOL Annex V.

evidence.excerpt:
11-1.3 Requirements
In order to comply with the functional requirement of paragraph 11-1.2
above, the master shall consider a route through polar waters, taking into
account the following:
          .1     the procedures required by the safety management
                 system on board; if no safety management system is
                 implemented there shall be a documented procedure for
                 operation in polar waters;
          .2     any limitations of the hydrographic information and aids
                 to navigation available;
          .3     current information on the extent and type of ice and
                 icebergs in the vicinity of the intended route;
          .4     statistical information on ice and temperatures from
                 former years;
          .5     places of refuge;
          .6     current information and measures to be taken when
                 marine mammals are encountered relating to known
                 areas with densities of marine mammals, including
                 seasonal migration areas;1
          .7     current information on relevant ships’ routeing systems,
                 speed recommendations and vessel traffic services
                 relating to known areas with densities of marine
                 mammals, including seasonal migration areas;1
          .8     national and international designated protected areas
                 along the route; and
          .9     operation in areas remote from search and rescue (SAR)
                 capabilities.2




1
  Refer to Guidance document for minimizing the risk of ship strikes with cetaceans
(MEPC/Circ.674).
2
  Refer to Enhanced contingency planning guidance for passenger ships operating
in areas remote from SAR facilities (MSC.1/Circ.1184) and Guidelines on voyage
planning for passenger ships operating in remote areas (resolution A.999(25)).”




6                   JANUARY 2026 SUPPLEMENT – POLAR CODE 2016 EDITION
                                           Resolution MSC.538(107)

evidence.excerpt:
11-1.3 Requirements
In order to comply with the functional requirement of paragraph 11-1.2
above, the master shall consider a route through polar waters, taking into
account the following:
          .1     the procedures required by the safety management
                 system on board; if no safety management system is
                 implemented there shall be a documented procedure for
                 operation in polar waters;
          .2     any limitations of the hydrographic information and aids
                 to navigation available;
          .3     current information on the extent and type of ice and
                 icebergs in the vicinity of the intended route;
          .4     statistical information on ice and temperatures from
                 former years;
          .5     places of refuge;
          .6     current information and measures to be taken when
                 marine mammals are encountered relating to known
                 areas with densities of marine mammals, including
                 seasonal migration areas;1
          .7     current information on relevant ships’ routeing systems,
                 speed recommendations and vessel traffic services
                 relating to known areas with densities of marine
                 mammals, including seasonal migration areas;1
          .8     national and international designated protected areas
                 along the route; and
          .9     operation in areas remote from search and rescue (SAR)
                 capabilities.2




1
  Refer to Guidance document for minimizing the risk of ship strikes with cetaceans
(MEPC/Circ.674).
2
  Refer to Enhanced contingency planning guidance for passenger ships operating
in areas remote from SAR facilities (MSC.1/Circ.1184) and Guidelines on voyage
planning for passenger ships operating in remote areas (resolution A.999(25)).”




6                   JANUARY 2026 SUPPLEMENT – POLAR CODE 2016 EDITION
                                           Resolution MSC.538(107)

PREFIX nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#>

    ?maxfq qudt:numericValue ?maxf .

    ?minfq qudt:numericValue ?minf .
    $this nltl:operatingAftDraught ?oaq .

    ?minaq qudt:numericValue ?mina .
    FILTER (
        ?of < ?minf ||
        ?of > ?maxf ||
        ?oa < ?mina ||

source_evidence.frozen_requirement_text: Restrictions on draughts when operating in ice shall be documented and kept on board readily available to the master. The maximum and minimum ice class draughts fore, amidships and aft shall be indicated in the class certificate. For ships built on or after 1 July 2007, if the summer load line in fresh water is anywhere located at a higher level than the UIWL, the ship's sides are to be provided with a warning triangle and with an ice class draught mark at the maximum permissible ice class draught amidships (see Annex III). Ships built before 1 July 2007 shall be provided with such a marking, if the UIWL is below the summer load line, not later than the first scheduled dry docking after 1 July 2007.

conditionalRules.if: constructionDate < 2007-07-01 AND complete required warning-triangle and ice-class-draught-mark evidence exists
conditionalRules.then: pass without requiring firstScheduledDryDockingDate

conditionalRules.then: require firstScheduledDryDockingDate; when firstScheduledDryDockingDate <= assessmentDate, require the markings

source_evidence.source_clause: 2.2 / equation (2.1) (LIWL loading, ballast freezing prevention, propeller submergence and forward draught)
source_evidence.frozen_requirement_text: The ship shall always be loaded down at least to the draught of LIWL amidships when navigating in ice. Any ballast tank, situated above the LIWL and needed to load down the ship to this water line, shall be equipped with devices to prevent the water from freezing. In determining the LIWL, regard shall be paid to the need to ensure a reasonable degree of ice-going capability in ballast. The highest point of the propeller shall be submerged and if possible at a depth of at least h_i below the water surface in all loading conditions. The forward draught shall be at least (2 + 0.00025*Delta)*h_i [m], but need not exceed 4*h_i (2.1), where Delta is the displacement of the ship [t] determined from the waterline on the UIWL (see section 2.1). Where multiple waterlines are used for determining the UIWL, the displacement must be determined from the waterline corresponding to the greatest displacement. h_i is the level ice thickness [m] according to section 4.2.1.

contract.comparisonModel: When navigating in ice, draught_amidships_m >= LIWL_draught_amidships_m. Any ballast tank above LIWL that is needed to reach LIWL shall have freezing_prevention_present = true. propeller_highest_point_submerged = true. forward_draught_m >= min((2 + 0.00025*displacement_UIWL_t)*level_ice_thickness_m, 4*level_ice_thickness_m). If multiple UIWL waterlines exist, use the displacement at the greatest-displacement UIWL.

source_evidence.frozen_requirement_text: To qualify for ice class IA Super, IA, IB or IC, a ship the keel of which is laid or which is at a similar stage of construction on or after 1 September 2003 shall comply with the following requirements regarding its engine output. The engine output requirement shall be calculated for two draughts by formula 3.1. Draughts to be used are the maximum draught amidships referred to as UIWL and the minimum draught amidships referred to as LIWL, as defined in section 2.2. In the calculations, the ship's parameters which depend on the draught must be determined at the appropriate draught, but L and B must be determined only at the UIWL. The engine output shall be no less than the greater of these two outputs. P_min = K_e*(R_CH/1000)^(3/2)/D_p [kW] (3.1), where K_e shall be given a value according to Table 3-1. Table 3-1 values for conventional propulsion systems: 1 propeller: CP propeller or electric or hydraulic propulsion machinery 2.03, FP propeller 2.26; 2 propellers: 1.44 and 1.60; 3 propellers: 1.18 and 1.31.

contract.comparisonModel: IF construction_stage_date >= '2003-09-01' AND iceClass IN {'IA Super','IA','IB','IC'}, THEN compute P_min = K_e*(R_CH/1000)^(3/2)/D_p at UIWL and LIWL; use draught-dependent inputs at the corresponding draught, use L and B at UIWL for both calculations, and require mcrPower_kW >= max(P_min_UIWL_kW, P_min_LIWL_kW). K_e shall be selected from Table 3-1. Table 3-1 values for conventional propulsion systems: 1 propeller: CP propeller or electric or hydraulic propulsion machinery 2.03, FP propeller 2.26; 2 propellers: 1.44 and 1.60; 3 propellers: 1.18 and 1.31.

source_evidence.frozen_requirement_text: To qualify for ice class IA Super, IA, IB or IC, a ship the keel of which is laid or which is at a similar stage of construction on or after 1 September 2003 shall comply with the following requirements regarding its engine output. Draughts to be used are the maximum draught amidships referred to as UIWL and the minimum draught amidships referred to as LIWL, as defined in section 2.2. In the calculations, the ship's parameters which depend on the draught must be determined at the appropriate draught, but L and B must be determined only at the UIWL. The engine output shall be no less than the greater of these two outputs. P_min = K_e*(R_CH/1000)^(3/2)/D_p [kW] (3.1), where K_e shall be given a value according to Table 3-1. Table 3-1 values for conventional propulsion systems: 1 propeller: CP propeller or electric or hydraulic propulsion machinery 2.03, FP propeller 2.26; 2 propellers: 1.44 and 1.60; 3 propellers: 1.18 and 1.31.

source_evidence.frozen_requirement_text: Direct analyses are to be carried out using the load patch defined in section 4.2 (p, h and la). The pressure to be used is 1.8p where p is determined according to 4.2.2. The load patch must be applied at locations where the capacity of the structure under the combined effects of bending and shear is minimised. In particular, the structure must be checked with a load centred at the UIWL, 0.5h0 below the LIWL, and positioned at several vertical locations in between. Several horizontal locations shall also be checked, especially the locations centred at the mid-span or -spacing. Furthermore, if the load length la cannot be determined directly from the arrangement of the structure, several values of la shall be checked using corresponding values for ca.

An ice-strengthened ship is assumed to operate in open sea conditions corresponding to a level
ice thickness not exceeding hi. The design ice load height (h) of the area actually under ice
pressure at any particular point of time is, however, assumed to be only a fraction of the ice
thickness. The values for hi and h are given in Table 4-1.

                     Table 4-1: Values of hi and h for the different ice classes
                             Ice Class           hi [m]           h [m]
                             IA Super               1.0            0.35
                             IA                     0.8            0.30
                             IB                     0.6            0.25
                             IC                     0.4            0.22


4.2.2       Ice pressure

The design ice pressure is determined by the formula:

                                      𝑝𝑝 = 𝑐𝑐𝑑𝑑 𝑐𝑐𝑝𝑝 𝑐𝑐𝑎𝑎 𝑝𝑝0 [MPa],                            (4.1)
evidence.review_note: All four Table4-1 hi/h cells reviewed: IA Super1/.35, IA .8/.30, IB .6/.25, IC .4/.22.

A longitudinal frame shall be attached by brackets to all supporting web frames and bulkheads. When a frame is running through the supporting structure, both sides of the web plate of the frame must be connected to the structure (by direct welding, collar plate or lug). When a bracket is installed, it must have at least the same thickness as the web plate of the frame and the edge must be appropriately stiffened against buckling.

TRF-052-F01.intended_rationale: Triggered anti-tripping support spacing exceeds 1300 mm.

source_evidence.frozen_requirement_text: Asymmetrical frames and frames which are not at right angles to the shell (web less than 90 degrees to the shell) shall be supported against tripping by brackets, intercoastals, stringers or similar, at a distance not exceeding 1,300 mm. For frames with spans greater than 4 m, the extent of antitripping supports must be applied to all regions and for all ice classes. For frames with spans less than or equal to 4 m, the extent of antitripping supports must be applied to all regions for ice class IA Super, to the bow and midbody regions for ice class IA, and to the bow region for ice classes IB and IC. Direct calculation methods may be applied to demonstrate the equivalent level of support provided by alternative arrangements.

contract.comparisonModel: IF frame_asymmetrical = true OR frame_web_angle_to_shell_deg < 90, THEN antitripping_support_spacing_mm <= 1300. IF frame_span_m > 4, THEN antitripping_support_scope = 'all regions/all ice classes'. IF frame_span_m <= 4, THEN required scope is all regions for IA Super, bow and midbody for IA, and bow for IB or IC. An alternative arrangement is acceptable only when equivalent_support_status_by_direct_calculation = demonstrated.

source_evidence.frozen_requirement_text: Asymmetrical frames and frames which are not at right angles to the shell (web less than 90 degrees to the shell) shall be supported against tripping by brackets, intercoastals, stringers or similar, at a distance not exceeding 1,300 mm. For frames with spans greater than 4 m, the extent of antitripping supports must be applied to all regions and for all ice classes. For frames with spans less than or equal to 4 m, the extent of antitripping supports must be applied to all regions for ice class IA Super, to the bow and midbody regions for ice class IA, and to the bow region for ice classes IB and IC. Direct calculation methods may be applied to demonstrate the equivalent level of support provided by alternative arrangements.

contract.comparisonModel: IF frame_asymmetrical = true OR frame_web_angle_to_shell_deg < 90, THEN antitripping_support_spacing_mm <= 1300. IF frame_span_m > 4, THEN antitripping_support_scope = 'all regions/all ice classes'. IF frame_span_m <= 4, THEN required scope is all regions for IA Super, bow and midbody for IA, and bow for IB or IC. An alternative arrangement is acceptable only when equivalent_support_status_by_direct_calculation = demonstrated.

source_evidence.frozen_requirement_text: These regulations apply to propulsion machinery covering open- and ducted-type propellers with a controllable pitch or fixed pitch design for ice classes IA Super, IA, IB and IC. The given propeller loads are the expected ice loads for the entire ship's service life under normal operational conditions, including loads resulting from the changing rotational direction of FP propellers. However, these loads do not cover off-design operational conditions, for example when a stopped propeller is dragged through ice. However, the load models of the regulations do not include propeller/ice interaction loads when ice enters the propeller of a turned azimuthing thruster from the side (radially).

contract.comparisonModel: The propulsion-machinery rule applies when iceClass IN {'IA Super','IA','IB','IC'} and propeller_type IN {'open','ducted'} and pitch_type IN {'controllable','fixed'}. The design-load scope shall cover normal service-life propeller/ice loads, including FP reversal loads, and shall record that stopped-propeller dragging and radial ice entry into a turned azimuthing thruster are outside the prescribed load-model scope.

intended.query:
PREFIX nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#>
            PREFIX qudt: <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/>
            PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>

            SELECT $this
            WHERE {
                $this nltl:iceClass ?iceClass .
                FILTER (?iceClass IN (nltl:iceClassIb, nltl:iceClassIc))

                $this nltl:ballastConditionPropellerTopDepth ?depthQuantity .
                ?depthQuantity qudt:numericValue ?depth .
                ?depthQuantity qudt:unit <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/M> .

                $this nltl:requiredPropellerSubmersionDepthHi ?hiQuantity .
                ?hiQuantity qudt:numericValue ?hi .
                ?hiQuantity qudt:unit <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/M> .

                FILTER (
                    datatype(?depth) = xsd:decimal &&
                    datatype(?hi) = xsd:decimal &&
                    ?depth < ?hi
                )

                FILTER NOT EXISTS {
                    $this nltl:propulsionSystemDesignedForIceClass nltl:iceClassIa .
                }
            }

Fb and Ff originate from different propeller/ice interaction phenomena, and do not occur simultaneously. Hence, they are to be applied to one blade separately.

source_evidence.frozen_requirement_text: For this purpose, at least one cooling water inlet chest shall be arranged as follows: 1. The sea inlet shall be situated near the centreline of the ship and well aft, if possible. 2. Guidance for designing the volume of the chest shall be around one cubic metre for every 750 kW in engine output of the ship, including the output of auxiliary engines necessary for the operation of the ship. 3. The chest shall be sufficiently high to allow ice to accumulate above the inlet pipe. 4. A pipe for discharge cooling water, allowing full capacity discharge, shall be connected to the chest. 5. The open area of the strainer plates shall be no less than four (4) times the inlet pipe sectional area. If there are difficulties in meeting the requirements of paragraphs 2 and 3 above, two smaller chests may be arranged for alternating the intake and discharge of cooling water. Otherwise, the arrangements and situation shall be as above. Heating coils may be installed in the upper part of the sea chest.

contract.comparisonModel: At least one cooling-water inlet chest shall satisfy: sea_inlet_location = near_centreline_and_well_aft_if_possible; recommended_chest_volume_m3 approximately total_relevant_engine_power_kW/750; ice_accumulation_space_above_inlet = true; full_capacity_discharge_pipe_connected = true; strainer_open_area_m2 >= 4*inlet_pipe_area_m2. If paragraphs 2 and 3 cannot be met, two smaller alternating intake/discharge chests may be used. Heating coils are optional.
contract.formulaExpression: For every inletChest, recommendedChestVolume is approximately totalRelevantEnginePower/750 and strainerOpenArea >= 4*inletPipeArea. At least one hasComponent object typed inletChest is required; if the volume/height selector is true, at least two smaller inletChest components with alternatingCoolingWaterIntakeAndDischarge true are required.
